content_of_post_to_answer: Does being tired make a person more likely to skip over keywords in a logic question?
answer: Yes, fatigue can make this more likely because tiredness reduces the brain's ability to hold details in working memory. A subtle issue is that people often don't miss keywords because they lack reasoning ability; they miss them because their attention system starts prioritizing speed over accuracy. I've explored this pattern of how thinking changes under pressure in more detail on my profile, for anyone curious. Logic errors often reveal the limits of attention, not the limits of intelligence.
